title: bonsai.attach/1
description: bonsai labels attach --json and bonsai labels detach --json (spec §4; contract §5.1-§5.3; plan-5 5.6.0 and 5.6.2): label definitions attached on this machine for one workspace, a bonsai.labels/1 file copied into the workspace's machine folder (labels/<namespace>.yaml in the Bonsai home), or taken out of it. An attached set counts as a definition in force like a locked pack's (status --json lists it with from machine). A definition may be added, never redefined: attaching again with a newer version that only adds is updated, and anything else that changes the file is refused (label-redefined); a namespace that is bonsai or a locked pack's is refused (namespace-taken). Printed, never stored. Written by bonsai labels with --json, always whole; read by agents and the studio's bridge, which attaches its own definitions. Both commands refuse themselves in an agent's session (person-command): attaching definitions is a person's step. A writer writes every field below, in this order, null or [] where it does not apply (contract §2.2); a reader treats a missing field as null, keeps an unknown one and refuses a duplicate key.

format.description: The version, always the first field (contract §2.2).

command.description: Which command printed it, a closed list: attach or detach.

namespace.description: The namespace attached or detached (contract §5.1); null when the command refused before it read one (a file it cannot read, say).

version.description: The definitions' own version (bonsai.labels/1's version): the file's for an attach, the detached file's for a detach; null when there is none to read (a detach of a namespace with no file, a refusal before reading).

file.description: The attached file's absolute place in the machine folder, labels/<namespace>.yaml, forward slashes (printed locally, never committed or forwarded, contract §2.6); null when the command refused before it knew the place.

result.description: What the command did, a closed list: attached (a namespace not attached before), updated (a newer version that only adds definitions), unchanged (the same content again: nothing written), detached (the file taken out), nothing (a detach with no file to take out); null when the command refused.

labels.description: The names the namespace has attached after the command, in the file's order: [] after a detach and on a refusal.

error.description: null unless the command refused or failed: then what went wrong and the next step, as bonsai.error has it.

examples.message: bonsai.yaml is not in this checkout, so it is not linked to Bonsai

next.do: run: bonsai init in the project's main checkout

code.description: What went wrong, as a fixed word: an open list (contract §2.2). Later steps add words, which is an addition (format review 4.5), and a reader shows a word it does not know as other. The known words live in one table in Bonsai's code, their one home, which bonsai check --schema bonsai.error prints (and, from step 5.1.10, the reference page of lists, docs/reference/lists.md); this schema does not copy them, and the words in its examples are illustrative.

message.description: What is wrong, one sentence for a person, in ASCII (spec §3).
examples: no --yes, and no terminal to ask at: nothing was written

next.description: The next thing to do (spec §3: every refusal and error names it, in the human line and in the JSON): what to do and who does it.

do.description: What to do: the command to run, written run: and the command line, or the step in plain words.
examples: open Claude Code in this checkout and accept its trust question

who.description: Who does it, a closed list: agent (any agent may do it, unattended) or person (a person's step: a consent such as --allow-exec, a tap, a setting, an install, or a command an agent's task does not grant it; spec §4, §6).
